_format: skill-creator eval format — see https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/evaluating-skills. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions.

evals.prompt: We just decided to switch the inventory service from MySQL to PostgreSQL because of JSONB and partitioning. Record that decision properly.
assertions: Creates the record under an ADR directory (docs/adr/ or the repo's existing corpus location)
Filename matches adr-NNNN-<kebab-title>.md with the next free number

Record contains MADR sections: Context and Problem Statement, Considered Options (chosen option listed first), Decision Outcome opening with 'Chosen option:', Consequences as Good/Bad-because bullets, and a Confirmation subsection naming a concrete check
Frontmatter status is lowercase (proposed or accepted) and date is the last-updated date
A row for the new record is appended to the index Records table
The consistency validator is run (or its absence is called out) after writing

evals.prompt: We reverted the decision in ADR-0007 last Tuesday — production couldn't handle the migration. Update our decision log to reflect reality.
assertions: Appends a dated More Information history bullet citing the revert (with commit reference when available) instead of rewriting the body
The original decision body text is left as decided
Creates a new superseding ADR for the reversal or sets status to superseded/deprecated with a forward link, per MADR supersession mechanics
The index row is updated to mirror the new status and date
Does not backdate: dates come from git history or the stated event, not invention

evals.prompt: Help me think through whether we should adopt Kafka or RabbitMQ for our event bus — I want to weigh the options.
assertions: Does NOT create an ADR for an unmade decision — frames the work as design exploration (RFC/design doc territory)
Offers to record an ADR only once a decision is actually made
